summary.one_liner: OpenWeb is an agent-native tool that accesses 90+ websites by calling their underlying APIs directly and returning structured JSON, instead of driving the browser DOM.
summary.what_it_does: It packages each website as a self-contained spec-driven site package (manifest, OpenAPI spec, adapters, examples, and agent-facing docs). The runtime builds each request, resolves auth (cookies, JWT, CSRF, signing) from the user's existing browser session, and dispatches it over HTTP, browser-backed fetch, SSR extraction, or WebSocket depending on the operation. Operations are typed with params, response schemas, and examples. Each operation is tagged read, write, delete, or transact, and permission tiers gate the non-read ones. SSRF protection is applied to each request. It is used via a CLI (npx @openweb-org/openweb) or as an agent skill, and the README describes a discovery workflow for adding new sites.
use_cases: query website data as structured JSON without screenshots
automate read-only lookups across social, shopping, or news sites
give an AI agent access to websites through their APIs
add a new website as an agent-callable API
gate write, delete, or purchase actions behind permissions
notable: Transport is chosen automatically per operation: direct HTTP, browser-backed fetch, SSR, or adapter/intercept
Auth is resolved locally from the existing browser session; no tokens handled by the caller
Each operation is tagged read/write/delete/transact with permission tiers
Agent-driven workflow to discover and add new sites, with 90+ built in
Packages declare auth and transport via x-openweb extensions in the OpenAPI spec
caveats: Tested on macOS with Google Chrome; Linux only lightly tested and Windows not yet tested
Write and delete operations need permission config, and sites may rate-limit or ban accounts that automate against them
